newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to give Medal of Freedom to Dole.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to give Medal of Freedom to Dole.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton will present former Republican rival Bob Dole with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian award, White House officials said on Wednesday.

Dole is scheduled to receive the award on Friday during a White House ceremony honouring veterans of the Second World War, administration officials said. Dole was twice decorated for heroism during the war and spent 39 months in hospitals recovering for wounds.

While declining to confirm or deny the decision to present Dole with the award, Deputy White House Press Secretary Mary Ellen Glynn said, "It sounds like an excellent way to pay tribute to a person who has devoted his life to public service."
Dole resigned in June as Senate Republican leader in order to concentrate full-time on his unsucessful challenge to deny Clinton a second term in the White House.
Clinton, who intends to stress a theme of healing when he delivers his inaugural address on Monday, wanted to honour the 73-year-old Dole's public service to the nation, officials said.

Dole was wounded as a U.S. Army second lieutenant in Italy as he led an assault on a German machinegun nest. After his lengthy recovery, he entered politics and won a House of Representatives seat in 1960 and a Senate seat in 1968.
